proofs.proof_tex:
Write the normalized time effects as \(\lambda_1=0\) and
\(\lambda_t\in\mathbb R\) for \(2\le t\le T\).  The assumed finite
existence of the individual PPML maximizer makes all first-order
conditions below necessary.  For fixed \(\lambda\), define, for every
\(g\in C\) and \(1\le i\le n_g\),
\[
 Q_{gi}:=\sum_{s<g}Y_{gis},
 \qquad
 L_g(\lambda):=\sum_{s<g}\exp(\lambda_s).
\]
Because \(g\in\{2,\ldots,T,\infty\}\), period \(1\) occurs in every sum
defining \(L_g\), and hence \(L_g(\lambda)>0\).  By nonnegativity of the
outcomes and the equal-weight, one-observation-per-period individual
criterion in the definition of \(\widehat\xi_{\mathrm{MK}}\), the part
of that criterion depending on \(\alpha_{gi}\) is
\[
 \ell_{gi}(\alpha_{gi};\lambda)
 =
 Q_{gi}\alpha_{gi}
 +\sum_{s<g}Y_{gis}\lambda_s
 -\exp(\alpha_{gi})L_g(\lambda).
\]
If \(Q_{gi}=0\), then
\(\partial\ell_{gi}/\partial\alpha_{gi}
=-\exp(\alpha_{gi})L_g(\lambda)<0\), so the supremum is approached
only as \(\alpha_{gi}\to-\infty\) and no finite maximizer exists.
The assumed existence of the individual fit therefore implies
\(Q_{gi}>0\).  Moreover,
\[
 \frac{\partial\ell_{gi}}{\partial\alpha_{gi}}
 =
 Q_{gi}-\exp(\alpha_{gi})L_g(\lambda),
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial^2\ell_{gi}}{\partial\alpha_{gi}^2}
 =
 -\exp(\alpha_{gi})L_g(\lambda)<0.
\]
Thus the unique profiled value and its fitted prediction are
\[
 \widehat\alpha_{gi}(\lambda)
 =
 \log Q_{gi}-\log L_g(\lambda),
 \qquad
 \exp\{\widehat\alpha_{gi}(\lambda)+\lambda_t\}
 =
 \frac{Q_{gi}\exp(\lambda_t)}{L_g(\lambda)}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Set \(\overline Q_g:=\sum_{s<g}\overline Y_{gs}\).  The definition of
\(\overline Y_g\) gives
\(\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}Q_{gi}=n_g\overline Q_g\), so summing (1) over
individuals yields, for every \(1\le t\le T\), including treated
periods,
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
 \exp\{\widehat\alpha_{gi}(\lambda)+\lambda_t\}
 =
 n_g\frac{\overline Q_g\exp(\lambda_t)}{L_g(\lambda)}.
 \tag{2}
\]

We next identify the time effect in (2).  By the definitions of \(X\)
and \(\beta\), write
\(x_{gt}^{\prime}\beta=\gamma_g+\lambda_t\), where
\(\gamma_g=\log a_g\) and \(\lambda_1=0\).  The cohort-intercept
component of the cohort-mean PPML equation
\(X^{\prime}\widehat P_U[\overline Y_U-\exp(X\beta)]=0\) is
\[
 0
 =
 \widehat p_g\sum_{s<g}
 \{\overline Y_{gs}-\exp(\gamma_g+\lambda_s)\}.
\]
Here \(\widehat p_g=n_g/N=p_g>0\) by the sample-share condition in the
proposition and the positive-share assumption.  Hence its unique
finite profiled cohort intercept satisfies
\[
 \exp\{\widehat\gamma_g(\lambda)\}
 =
 \frac{\overline Q_g}{L_g(\lambda)},
 \qquad
 \widetilde\mu_{gt}(\lambda)
 :=
 \exp\{\widehat\gamma_g(\lambda)+\lambda_t\}
 =
 \frac{\overline Q_g\exp(\lambda_t)}{L_g(\lambda)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
At the finite individual maximizer, the score for each unrestricted
\(\lambda_t\), \(2\le t\le T\), is zero.  Substitution of (2), followed
by division by \(N>0\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0
 &=
 \frac1N\sum_{g:\,t<g}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
 \left[
 Y_{git}
 -
 \exp\{\widehat\alpha_{gi}(\lambda)+\lambda_t\}
 \right] \\
 &=
 \sum_{g:\,t<g}\frac{n_g}{N}
 \left[
 \overline Y_{gt}
 -
 \frac{\overline Q_g\exp(\lambda_t)}{L_g(\lambda)}
 \right] \\
 &=
 \sum_{g:\,t<g}p_g
 \{\overline Y_{gt}-\widetilde\mu_{gt}(\lambda)\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
Equation (4) is exactly the time-coordinate of the cohort-mean PPML
score after profiling its cohort intercepts by (3).  Conversely, (3)
and (4) jointly give every coordinate of the cohort-mean score.
Therefore the normalized time component of the individual fit is a
normalized solution of the cohort-mean score equations.  The
stipulated uniqueness of both normalized fits implies that this time
component equals the time component of \(\widehat\beta\).  Equations
(2) and (3), evaluated at that common solution, consequently prove
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}
 =
 n_g\widehat\mu_{gt}
 \qquad
 (g\in C,\ 1\le t\le T).
 \tag{5}
\]

It remains to compare the reported ratios rather than merely their
fitted means.  The treated-support assumption gives
\(D\ne\varnothing\).  Since \(n_g\ge1\), \(p_g>0\), and every
exponential fitted value is strictly positive, both treated
imputation denominators are strictly positive; thus the
positive-denominator branches in the two estimator definitions
apply.  Using \(n_g=Np_g\), the definition of \(\widehat A\), and then
(5) and the definition of \(\widehat B\), respectively, gives
\[
 \sum_{(g,t)\in D}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}Y_{git}
 =
 \sum_{(g,t)\in D}n_g\overline Y_{gt}
 =
 N\sum_{(g,t)\in D}p_g\overline Y_{gt}
 =
 N\widehat A,
 \tag{6}
\]
\[
 \sum_{(g,t)\in D}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
 \widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}
 =
 \sum_{(g,t)\in D}n_g\widehat\mu_{gt}
 =
 N\sum_{(g,t)\in D}p_g\widehat\mu_{gt}
 =
 N\widehat B.
 \tag{7}
\]
Cancellation of the common positive factor \(N\) in (6)--(7) proves
\[
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}
 =
 \frac{N\widehat A}{N\widehat B}-1
 =
 \widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}},
\]
as claimed.  This is a deterministic sample identity; the
within-cohort sampling assumption is not needed for the algebra.

proposed.statement: Suppose both normalized PPML fits exist uniquely, the panel contains one observation per unit and period, the Moreau--Kastler fit uses equal observation weights with no covariates or offsets, and \(n_g/N=p_g\) for every \(g\in C\). Profiling its individual fixed effects gives the cohort-mean PPML time-score equations and \(\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{MK}}_{git}=n_g\widehat\mu_{gt}\); consequently \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{MK}}^{\mathrm{ind}}=\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{CM}}\).
proposed.justification: The boundary result states the exact aggregation conditions under which the distinct individual and cohort-mean procedures coincide.
proposed.gap: Moreau--Kastler (2025, Appendix B2) links individual imputation to a fully interacted individual-level estimator; it does not state this profiling identity with the cohort-mean rank-one score used here.
proposed.consumer: Applied users can determine whether the cycle frontier transfers exactly to their implementation or only describes a cohort-mean benchmark.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The ratio conclusion uses \(D\ne\varnothing\) to ensure that the strictly positive exponential predictions are summed over at least one treated cell. Without that condition the Moreau--Kastler ratio is outside its positive-denominator domain, so the existing frozen treated-support assumption must be declared in this proposition's proof spine.
